positions.claim: Engineers spend about 70% of their time running code in production rather than writing it, per a survey study.
Writing code was never the real engineering bottleneck; operating systems in production is.
AI-generated code is increasing the volume of production issues, and existing organizational structures are not equipped for the resulting change rate.
The era of effectively unlimited tokens is ending — prices are rising and companies are becoming more stringent about AI spend.
Model capability is no longer the limiting factor for production agents; capturing and maintaining an understanding of the specific environment is.
Production context matters more than execution capability for background agents.
Standard CI/CD checks are good baselines but are not exhaustive, because every rollout is unique and needs different signals watched.
Feature flags and infrastructure changes frequently bypass CI/CD and receive no monitoring at all.
AI agents should augment rather than replace existing CI/CD pipelines.
An agent that dynamically reasons about what changed and builds a per-release check plan catches problems that fixed hard-coded checks and wait intervals miss.
Agents should be embedded in the tools engineers already use, like Slack and MS Teams, rather than requiring people to visit a separate product UI.
Every company's environment is unique enough that a generic agent cannot be effective without a per-customer knowledge system.
